assumptions: The FASTA is in-frame CDS records, as NCBI writes `cds_from_genomic.fna`.
Highly-expressed means the ribosomal proteins, recognized from the record headers.
limits: HEG mode selects by HEADER text: a FASTA whose deflines do not name genes has no ribosomal proteins to find, and the refusal says so rather than returning the genome table under the HEG label.
An amino acid absent from the HEG set is backfilled from the whole genome, and every backfilled residue is named.
bio.jane/contract.question: What codon usage does this genome show, across its highly-expressed genes or all of them?

description: Build a codon-usage table from a genome's CDS FASTA (an NCBI `cds_from_genomic.fna`): either from its highly-expressed genes — the ribosomal proteins, which is what a codon-optimization reference table means — or from every CDS in the genome.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

fasta.description: or the CDS FASTA itself, in frame, one record per CDS.

file.description: the CDS FASTA to read, by name, from the project or the `_files` sent with the call. Empty reads the only FASTA there.

mode.description: `heg` builds the table from the ribosomal-protein genes, which is the reference set a codon-optimization table means. `genome` uses every CDS, which is the honest choice for a plasmid or any corpus whose highly-expressed genes are not in it. Values: heg (Highly-expressed genes (ribosomal proteins)), genome (Every CDS in the corpus).

name: build_codon_table_from_cds

backfilled.description: amino acids absent from the highly-expressed set, taken from the whole genome instead. Empty in genome mode

cdsTotal.description: CDS records read from the corpus

cdsUsed.description: CDS records that went into the table

gc3.description: GC at the third codon position of the reference set, the usual summary of a genome’s codon bias

mode.description: which reference set this table was built from

tsv.description: the usage table as a Kazusa-style TSV — wire it into optimize_sequence, codon_usage_analysis or design_expression_variants
